newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran official denies reforms based on IMF advice.
newsitem.headline: Iran official denies reforms based on IMF advice.

text.p: A senior Iranian official on Thursday denied any of Iran's economic liberalisation reforms were based on recommendations by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"Contrary to the view expressed by some, the economic programmes carried out in the country have been independently designed and implemented by the Iranian government and are in no way influenced by the World Bank and the IMF," Mohammad Khazaei, Iran's envoy to the bank, told the daily Resalat.

He did not name any critics, but Iran's hardline politicians and newspapers condemn the World Bank and the IMF as bodies run by Tehran's arch-enemy Washington and say following their recipes would jeopardise the Islamic republic's independence.

Khazaei said Iran had, for example, rejected suggestions by the World Bank to raise electricity rates. "We did not follow their view in order to safeguard our national interests and to decrease pressure on consumers," he said.
Iran has cut some subsidies as part of its market reforms which also include the privatisation of some state firms, but fuel and power remain heavilly subsidised.

Khazaei said Iran had received $848.9 million in loans from the World Bank in a three-year period ending in March 1993. "In getting loans for these projects we have tried not to agree to conditions that the World Bank imposes because of its economic nature," he said.
Iran had borrowed no money from the IMF because Tehran refused to accept the recommendations it attached to its loans, Khazaei added.
IMF officials said in December Iran looked set to enjoy better economic times despite U.S. sanctions, but it still needed to carry out tough reforms to put its economy on a sounder long-run footing.
The IMF was providing Iran with technical advice, but did not have a loan deal with the country and there were no plans for one, they said.
The United States has in the past few years pressured Iran, which it accuses of sponsoring terrorism, by vetoing IMF and World Bank loans to Tehran. Iran denies the charge.
